title: Datetime gaps: no date-to-epoch conversion, date_add discards your format, date_diff has no month/year units
existing_state: epoch() ignores its arguments entirely and always returns the current Unix time (Services/Scripting/Functions/DateTimeFunctions.cs:52-55), so the inverse of epoch_to_date does not exist — you cannot convert a parsed log timestamp to epoch for arithmetic or comparison with device uptime counters. date_add accepts any input format from the ParseFormats list but always emits hardcoded 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss' (line 105) with no output-format argument (parse_date and epoch_to_date both already take one, lines 68-73 and 162-168 — date_add is the odd one out). date_diff supports seconds through weeks only; 'months' or 'years' silently falls into the default arm and returns seconds (lines 122-130). Also, now() and now_local() are byte-identical local-time implementations (lines 37-45) — a trap for anyone assuming now() is UTC like most scripting environments.
recommendation: In DateTimeFunctions: make epoch(ts?) parse an optional timestamp via the existing TryParseDateTime and return its Unix seconds (no arg keeps current behavior); add an optional 4th output-format arg to date_add matching the parse_date convention; add months/years arms to date_diff using calendar arithmetic; and document explicitly in SCRIPTING.md that now() is local (or add a one-line note in the function's autocomplete description once that exists).
user_benefit: Time math against device logs is constant in this domain — 'alert if last config save is older than 7 days' currently requires no clean path because you cannot get an epoch from a parsed date, and date_add silently reformatting timestamps breaks downstream parse_date calls.

evidence.note: Epoch ignores argsString — no date→epoch conversion exists
date_add output format hardcoded; unknown unit silently returns input
date_diff: months/years fall to default seconds arm
now and now_local are identical local-time implementations
